focus: Focus on the results at 2 and 4 weeks.
modelNote:
Create a clean, professional portrait infographic for a university student who has just read the research paper. Title at top: “Time management training: results at 2 and 4 weeks”. Subtitle: “Häfner, Stock & Oberst (2015) • undergraduate students • n = 23 for main analyses”.

Use ONLY the paper’s information below. Do not add external facts or extra claims. Spell everything correctly. Use a tall portrait layout, clear hierarchy, large readable text, icons, simple line/arrow charts. Every number shown must be exactly as reported.

Overall visual style: university handout, white background, navy and teal accents, simple icons (clock, student, stress bolt/cloud, control dial, clipboard). No tiny dense text. Prefer fewer larger blocks.

Infographic structure:

1) Header block
Title: “Time management training: results at 2 and 4 weeks”
Small citation line: “Decreasing students’ stress through time management training: an intervention study”

2) Small “Study snapshot” row with icons
- “48 students began”
- “23 completed all questionnaires”
- “4 h training”
- “Measured: directly before, 2 weeks after, 4 weeks after”
- “No control group; non-equivalent dependent variable design”
Keep this compact.

3) “What changed after training?” main section, focused on three outcomes. Use three stacked mini-panels with simple 3-point line charts from Time 1 to Time 2 to Time 3. Label x-axis: “Before”, “2 weeks”, “4 weeks”. Show means exactly. Use no invented percentages or calculated differences.

Panel A: “Perceived stress: tension”
Under title: “Significantly lower at 2 and 4 weeks”
Line chart values:
Before M = 3.30
2 weeks M = 2.96
4 weeks M = 3.03
Add small stats callouts:
“2 weeks: F(1, 22) = 8.22, partial η² = 0.27, p < 0.01”
“4 weeks: F(1, 22) = 5.75, partial η² = 0.21, p = 0.03”
Use stress icon trending downward.

Panel B: “Perceived control of time”
Under title: “Tendency at 2 weeks; significant increase at 4 weeks”
Line chart values:
Before M = 2.75
2 weeks M = 2.89
4 weeks M = 3.05
Add stats callouts:
“2 weeks: F(1, 22) = 3.38, partial η² = 0.13, p = 0.08”
“4 weeks: F(1, 22) = 11.62, partial η² = 0.35, p < 0.01”
Use control dial icon trending upward.

Panel C: “Demands: perceived, self-reported demands”
Under title: “No significant change”
Line chart values:
Before M = 3.59
2 weeks M = 3.35
4 weeks M = 3.46
Add stats callouts:
“2 weeks: t(22) = 1.68, p = 0.107”
“4 weeks: t(22) = 1.19, p = 0.251”
Use clipboard icon and neutral gray line.

4) “Transfer of time-management behaviour” side or lower section
Use small upward arrow chart or badge:
Values: Before M = 3.01; 2 weeks M = 3.19; 4 weeks M = 3.31
Text: “Reported use of taught strategies increased significantly by 4 weeks and was nearly significant at 2 weeks.”
Stats:
“2 weeks: t(22) = 1.62, p = 0.060, ε′ = 0.48”
“4 weeks: t(22) = 2.67, p < 0.01, ε′ = 0.79”

5) “How to read the pattern” conclusion section at bottom
Use concise text with icons:
- “At 2 weeks: stress was significantly lower; perceived control of time showed a tendency in the expected direction.”
- “At 4 weeks: stress was significantly lower and perceived control of time was significantly higher.”
- “Demands did not significantly change, supporting the authors’ interpretation that the training led to the intended changes.”

6) Small “Main limitation” footer
Text: “Preliminary study: small sample; no control group. The authors call for more intervention studies with larger samples.”

Important wording rules:
- Name perceived stress as “tension”.
- Name demands as “perceived, self-reported demands”.
- Use “significant” only where stated above.
- Do not say the training proves anything. Use: “supporting the authors’ interpretation”.
- Do not add data from cited studies.
- Do not calculate or display differences.

Make the infographic visually balanced, with readable type and correctly rendered statistical notation including η² and ε′.
